messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert fired: routing-service-high-error-rate
incident-bot: alert_id=PD0001234 severity=P2 service=routing-proxy-prod environment=prod
jen: acked via PD console :white_check_mark:
jen: I'm on it, pulling dashboards
matt: seeing a tight 30s spike of 5xx from the canary traffic generator in us-west-2, error-rate ~12% -> baseline 0.3%
mike: same, traced to canary payloads (large batch requests). No user traffic pattern matching this.
jen: good, that suggests synthetic noise rather than real customer traffic. tagging as potential flapping.
jen: @matt can you pause the canary and watch for regression?
matt: pausing canary now
matt: command:
```
./canary control pause --env prod --region us-west-2 --id canary-accessor-42
```
matt: paused. dropping requests immediately :arrow_down:
sam: I put a soft-silence on PD for 10m while we validate, so it won't escalate :lock:
jen: thanks. checking p95 latency and error budget - p95 steady, only the 30s 5xx blip
mike: logs show a timeout from the test runner to the test harness during that window, 504s stacking for retries
jen: sounds like test harness flapped. no customer-facing 5xx in front-door metrics. marking as no-customer-impact for now :ok_hand:
incident-bot: PagerDuty: alert auto-resolved (signal cleared) :white_check_mark:
jen: metrics are back to baseline for 3 full minutes. I'll close the on-call doc note and file a ticket to tune canary thresholds.
matt: filing follow-up ticket INC-4321 with timeline, payload sample, and suggested threshold increase
mike: proposed fix: increase canary timeout to 10s and require 5 consecutive failures before page
sam: added short writeup to #runbooks/canary-runbook and put owners tag @mike @matt
jen: no customer impact, short-lived noisy page, root cause: synthetic harness timeout. action items: (1) adjust thresholds (2) add builder-side retry backoff (3) monitor for recurrence
jen: handing off to next-shift @katie — please monitor for any re-occurrence over next 24h. thanks team :coffee:
katie: ack, I'll watch dashboards and follow INC-4321 in the morning :eyes:
matt: closing thread. :thumbsup:
